talk: After a buyout, the company uses its spare cash to pay down the debt. Every dollar repaid is a dollar more for the owners when the company is sold, even if the business doesn't grow at all. It's the quiet engine of private equity returns.

terms.meaning: Cash left after running costs, tax and investment, available to repay debt.

questions.prompt: A club is worth $50M and has $30M of debt. What's the owners' equity worth?
whyNot: $30M is the debt, which belongs to the lenders.
$50M is the whole club. The debt comes off first.
$50M + $30M = $80M adds the debt. It comes off.

questions.prompt: The club makes $4M of free cash flow a year and uses all of it to repay debt. After 5 years, how much debt is left?
questions.hint: Years times cash flow, off the debt.
whyNot: The cash flow goes to paying the debt down.
$20M is how much was repaid, not what's left.

questions.prompt: The club is still worth $50M after those 5 years. What's the owners' equity worth now?
working: $40M / $20M = 2, so the owners doubled their money without the club growing at all.
whyNot: The $10M of debt left still comes off.
$20M was before the debt was repaid.

penalty.prompt: A club worth {value} has {debt} of debt. It uses {fcf} of free cash flow a year to repay debt for {years} years. If it's still worth {value}, what's the owners' equity worth then?
penalty.hint: Work out the debt left, then take it off the value.
working: {debt} - {years * fcf|usd} = {debt - years * fcf|usd} of debt left.
{value} - {debt - years * fcf|usd} = {value - (debt - years * fcf)|usd} for the owners.

traps.why: That's before any debt was repaid.
The {debt - years * fcf|usd} of debt left still comes off.

call.title: Spare cash
call.prompt: The club has $1M of spare cash and a bank loan. Each $1M of the loan costs $2,500 a matchday in interest. Repay $1M of the loan, pay a $1M bonus to the owners (you get your share), or keep the cash in the bank.

options.label: Repay $1M of debt
options.result: Good call. It saves $2,500 a matchday in interest, and every dollar of debt repaid is a dollar more for the owners when the club is sold.

options.label: Pay a $1M owners' bonus
options.result: The money leaves the club. You get your share now, but the interest keeps running on the loan.

options.label: Keep it in the bank
options.result: Cash in the bank earns nothing here while the loan costs $2,500 a matchday.

takeaway: Paying down debt grows the owners' slice, even when the business stands still.
